title: Introduce hybrid remote build cache and parallel dependency resolution to reduce cold-build latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We observe frequent cold build spikes across CI agents caused by non-deterministic dependency resolution and missing cache hits for large monorepo images. Cold builds increase developer iteration time and CI cost. This ticket scopes a two-part solution: 1) a hybrid remote build cache layer (local disk warm cache + global remote content-addressable cache) that is transparent to existing buildkite steps and Docker build flows; 2) parallelized deterministic dependency resolution for our Node, Python, and Go toolchains to avoid serialized network resolution and flaky transitive updates. The plan includes a small runtime shim to rewrite build graph edges for cache keys, canonicalize dependency lockfiles at cache boundaries, and a change to CI agent startup to prefetch prioritized artifacts for high-traffic branches.

Implementation notes: We will prototype with BuildKit's remote cache export/import and integrate a Redis-backed priority queue for prefetch jobs. For dependency resolution we will adopt pnpm lockfile normalization for JS, pin pip-tools workflow for Python wheels, and enable go.sum verification with a per-agent module proxy cache. All changes must be backwards-compatible and toggled via feature flags in the pipeline config.

Goals: reduce median cold-build wall time by 40%, reduce repeated dependency downloads by 60%, and lower average CI CPU/GPU provisioning timeouts caused by long image pulls. Rollout is staged: prototype on dev runners, pilot on CI beta (desktop team), then org-wide enablement with telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Hybrid remote cache integrated in at least two BuildKit-based pipelines and exported artifacts validated for reproducibility
Cold-build median time reduced by >= 40% on our benchmark suite (monorepo: frontend, infra, runtime) measured over 72h
Dependency resolution parallelization reduces repeated external downloads by >= 60% for Node/Python/Go workloads
No regression in build artifact correctness; representative smoke tests pass on every cache hit and miss
Feature flags implemented and rollout plan documented in Confluence; ops runbook created for cache eviction and debugging
updates: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial spike analysis completed; attached cold-build flamegraphs and benchmark baseline (see attachments). Decided to prototype with BuildKit remote exporter + s3-backed CAS.

2026-02-20 - Marco Ruiz: Proof-of-concept BuildKit exporter working on local runner; achieved 18% cold build reduction in synthetic test. Found issue: Docker layer non-determinism from dev-only files - added canonical .dockerignore rules and a pre-build sanitization step.
2026-02-28 - Engineering sync: Chose pnpm normalization for JS lockfiles and pip-tools for Python. Action: create migration PRs for key repos to add lockfile validation in pre-commit.
2026-03-06 - Design review: Opted for two-tier cache TTLs (hot=24h, warm=7d) and LRU eviction on edge agents. Security requested S3 bucket encryption and read-restrictions; security review scheduled.
2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented prefetch queue prototype using Redis; observed 52% reduction in repeated downloads for a 24h window on pilot runners.

2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Opened PRs for BuildKit plugin and CI pipeline changes (see attachments). Staging rollout planned for 2026-03-18 after canary validation. Follow-ups: add more telemetry to measure tokenized cache hit rate by branch.
